name: UserMenu
description: The avatar button that opens the account menu: the person's name and email at the top, your own entries (settings, billing, help) in groups, a row for the theme, and a Sign out entry that can ask first, shows that it is working, and tells screen readers how it went.

user.description: The signed-in person: name (also the accessible name), email and the picture. Without a picture the initials are shown.
user.tsType: { name: string; email?: string; avatarUrl?: string }

items.description: Entries above Sign out: { id, label, icon?, href?, onSelect?, permission?, variant? }. An entry with an href is a link; without one it is a button that calls onSelect. permission is "allow", "disabled", "hidden" or { state, reason }: hidden entries are not drawn, disabled ones are shown dimmed with the reason beside them.

groups.description: More entries in groups, each with an optional heading. A separator is drawn between groups, and before Sign out.

themeRow.description: A row under the entries for choosing the theme, for example your segmented control. It sits below the menu inside the same popover and is reached with Tab.

onSignOut.description: Adds the Sign out entry and does the work. May be async. While it runs the entry shows it is pending; a throw or rejection is an error. Call your own sign-out API here; the library does not.

confirm.description: Ask before signing out. Opens an alert dialog, for example { title: "Sign out of Loomworks?" }; its confirm button runs onSignOut.
confirm.tsType: { title: string; description?: string; confirmLabel?: string }

signOutLabel.description: Text of the Sign out entry.

signingOutLabel.description: Text of the entry while the sign-out is running.

signedOutMessage.description: Announced politely when the sign-out succeeds. It is spoken from a status region that stays on the page after the menu closes.

errorMessage.description: Announced politely when the sign-out fails.
errorMessage.default: Could not sign out. Try again.

onSignedOut.description: Called after a successful sign-out, with what onSignOut returned. Usually where you go to the sign-in page.

onError.description: Called with the error when onSignOut throws or rejects.

permissions.description: What the person may do: { signOut } as "allow" (default), "disabled" or "hidden", or { state, reason }. The server must check again.

align.description: Which edge of the button the menu lines up with.

showName.description: Show the name and email beside the picture in the button. Use it where there is room, such as a sidebar.

label.description: Start of the button's accessible name. The person's name is added: "Account menu, Ada Lovelace".

classNames.description: Class names for the parts, by slot name, added after the built-in ones. Slots: root, trigger, avatar, name, popover, header, list, item, separator, theme, status.

keyboard: Enter, Space or Arrow Down on the button: opens the menu
Arrow keys: move between entries; Home and End: first and last
Enter or Space: chooses an entry
Escape: closes the menu and returns focus to the button
Tab (with a theme row): moves from the menu to the controls in the row
requirements: The button is named with the person's name ("Account menu, Ada Lovelace"); the picture is decorative
The menu is a real menu named by the person's name; the entries are menu items or links
Closing the menu returns focus to the button
Sign out: while it runs the entry says so and a second choice is ignored; the result is announced politely from a status region that stays after the menu closes, not by moving focus
With confirm, the alert dialog traps focus, starts on the safe choice, and focus returns to the button when it closes
A disabled entry says why in text beside it, not only in a tooltip
A destructive entry is shown in the danger color and also says what it does in words
screenReader: "Account menu, Ada Lovelace, menu button, collapsed"
"Ada Lovelace, menu", then each entry: "Settings, menu item"
"Signing out..." while pending, then "You have signed out" or "Could not sign out. Try again." as a status message

use_when: The top-right corner of an app: who is signed in, account entries and Sign out
At the bottom of a sidebar, with showName
avoid_when: A menu of actions on a record: use Menu
Switching organisations or workspaces: use the team switcher of Sidebar
anti_patterns: Doing the sign-out yourself in onSelect of an item: use onSignOut so it gets pending, the message and the confirmation
Putting more than about 7 entries in the menu
UI permission is not security: hiding or disabling an entry only changes what people see, so the server must check again for every request

contract.data: The signed-in person (name, email, picture) and the menu entries as plain data.
